patch.value: A budget-truncated read is resumable on one surface and terminal on five, and the only recovery the envelope names is to abandon the budget that truncated it

Every bounded read declares two truncation mechanisms and only one of them is resumable, but the envelope reports both through the same flag pair, so a caller cannot tell a page it can continue from a page it cannot.

## What is measured

At HEAD build 2026.8.14, on this 2,482-item workspace.

When the row limit is what truncates, the envelope carries a usable continuation cursor:

    pm list --status open --limit 10 --json
      -> count 10, has_more true, truncated true,
         next_cursor "eyJ2ZXJzaW9uIjoxLCJmaW5nZXJwcmludCI6ImVjMzAy..."

When the token budget is what truncates, the same three flags are set and the cursor is null:

    pm list --status open --limit 500 --json
      -> count 85 of total 343, has_more true, truncated true,
         next_cursor null,
         output_budget_truncation.reason "output_budget_reached"
         output_budget_truncation.restore_with
           "Re-run with --output-budget unbounded for the complete result."

The two cases are distinguishable only by reaching into output_budget_truncation, a key that is absent on the resumable case. Nothing in the flag pair the pagination contract is written against separates them.

## The population this makes unreadable

The surface that serves the historical record is the worst case measured:

    pm list-closed --limit 3000 --json
      -> 4 rows of total 2125, has_more true, next_cursor null

Four rows of 2,125 is 0.19 percent of the population, and the only recovery the envelope names is to abandon the budget:

    default budget      28,073 bytes    ~7,018 tokens     4 rows
    --output-budget unbounded  15,918,262 bytes  ~3,979,565 tokens  2125 rows
    amplification       567x

There is no intermediate. A caller that needs row 5 must either accept a 3.98 million token response or give up. At the declared million-item scale target the ratio is not a constant, and the prescribed recovery is the exact behaviour the budget exists to prevent.

## Why this is not the sibling that already shipped

pm-jt8aa2 closed on 2026-08-13 having shipped the disclosure block quoted above. Its third acceptance criterion reads: "has_more true is never emitted without either a usable continuation cursor or a named alternative recovery path". The disjunction is satisfied by restore_with, so the item is correctly closed on its own terms. This item owns the half the disjunction permitted: the named alternative is the only alternative, and it is unbounded.

## The inconsistency that proves it is not a design constraint

One command already does it correctly. Under the identical reason code, pm context emits both:

    pm context --limit 50 --json
      -> has_more true,
         output_budget_truncation.reason "output_budget_reached",
         next_cursor "eyJ2ZXJzaW9uIjoxLCJmaW5nZXJwcmludCI6IjllZDJm..."

Measured across the read surfaces:

    surface        budget-truncated   cursor emitted
    list                 yes               no
    list-open            yes               no
    list-all             yes               no
    list-closed          yes               no
    next                 yes               no
    context              yes              YES
    search               no (limit)       YES

So a budget-truncated read can carry a continuation cursor. Five surfaces do not, and the one that does proves the capability exists in the same code path.

## Collateral damage observed in this session

The defect is not confined to item listing. Reading this project's own quality gate under the default budget silently reshaped the measurement:

    pm assurance run tracker-context-quality --trigger ci --dry-run --json --output-budget 600
      -> verdict "pass", exit_code 0, assertions array length 2

    pm assurance run tracker-context-quality --trigger ci --dry-run --json --output-budget unbounded
      -> verdict "pass", exit_code 0, assertions array length 40

The scalar verdict was correct in both readings. The evidence set behind it was reduced by 95 percent with has_more carrying the only signal and no way to continue. A reviewer reading the budgeted form concludes the gate enforces two invariants when it enforces forty.

## Why the fix belongs to the budget contract

A cursor is a position in a total order. The budget truncation already knows the position at which it stopped compacting rows, because it names the compacted row paths. Emitting a cursor there is the same operation the limit path already performs. The contract question is what a continuation means when the budget rather than the caller chose the page size, and that is the declaration pm-5t33or owns, which is why this is ordered behind it.

A read truncated by the output budget emits a continuation cursor that resumes the same query at the first withheld row, on every row-producing surface that emits has_more; The envelope distinguishes limit truncation from budget truncation in the pagination contract itself, so a caller reading only the declared pagination keys can tell a resumable page from a terminal one; No recovery instruction for a budget truncation names an unbounded re-read as the sole path, and the declared recovery cost is bounded by a stated multiple of the budget rather than by the corpus; A regression test walks pm list-closed to completion on a workspace larger than the default budget using only cursors, and asserts total rows delivered equals total, with peak response size bounded; The assurance verdict surface is covered by the same contract, so a gate reading its own evidence rows under a budget either receives every assertion or receives a cursor to the rest
